title: The fire
hook: described so people turn back in time

segments.voice: Yesterday, hawd, the Prophet's pool, and your line: the pool. Did you pause for a breath before a sip of water? Today, the hardest picture in this part of the path. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-three.

A sign on a mountain road: sharp bend ahead, slow down. Nobody puts that sign there to frighten drivers for fun. It's there because someone wants them to make the turn. The Qur'an speaks of the fire in plain, hard language. Readers who come to it for the first time sometimes stop there. But the Qur'an itself says why the warning is given, and the hadith add a surprising detail about how small the way out can be. Today, the fire: what it is described for.
screen: `A SIGN BEFORE THE BEND.` → `HARD LANGUAGE.` → `WHY THE WARNING?`

segments.voice: In Arabic the fire is simply an-nar, the fire, and the Qur'an also gives it other names. Muslims hold it as real, part of the unseen they believe in, alongside the pool and the garden. The descriptions are not soft. But look at how the Qur'an frames them. In one passage, after describing the fire, it says that this is how Allah warns His servants, and then turns straight to them: so be mindful of Me. The picture comes with an address. It's spoken to people who still have time. That's the thread through today's lesson: the warning exists so that someone turns back while turning back is still possible. The Qur'an also draws a line. It says forgiveness is for those who do wrong in ignorance and then turn back soon, and it is not for the one who keeps on doing evil until death arrives and only then says, now I repent. So the warning is about timing. Turn back in time. Now the surprising detail. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet, peace be upon him, tells people to protect themselves from the fire, even with half a date given in charity. Half a date. Not a fortune, not a lifetime of perfection. Half a piece of fruit given to someone hungry. And another report adds: if you don't have even that, then with a kind word. So the same tradition that describes the fire in hard language also makes the door out of it very small and very near. Muslim scholars have discussed the fire's nature in detail, and they don't all agree on every question about it. But on the purpose of the warning, the text is clear. It's a sign before the bend.
screen: `AN-NAR: DESCRIBED IN HARD LANGUAGE.` · `A WARNING, SPOKEN TO THE LIVING.` · `TURN BACK BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE.` · then, large: `EVEN WITH HALF A DATE.`

segments.voice: The practice: turn back from one wrong. Settle, and breathe. Let one small wrong come to mind, something you've been doing lately that you'd rather not keep doing. A sharp word you keep using, a habit, a corner you keep cutting. Keep it small, and keep it honest. You don't need to judge yourself. Just picture the bend in the road, and picture taking the turn: one concrete thing you'll do differently today. If you pray, you can ask Allah for forgiveness in your own words. If not, simply hold the decision. The bell holds the time.
The fire. An-nar: described in the Qur'an in hard language, as a warning spoken to people who still have time to turn back. Today's word.
Your line: turn back in time. Today, give something small, half a snack, a coin, or a kind word, to someone who could use it. Tomorrow, the garden. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims affirm the fire as part of belief in the Last Day; some teachers present its descriptions alongside the hadith about protecting oneself even with half a date in charity, and Muslims ask Allah's forgiveness for wrongs they turn away from.

fork.setup: you want to protect yourself from the fire, but you have almost nothing to give. what does the hadith say?
options: wait until you can give a lot.
fork.reveal: in Bukhari the Prophet says to protect yourselves from the fire even with half a date in charity, and if not that, with a kind word.

trapdoor: what you thought: the fire is there to frighten people.
what it means: a warning spoken to the living, so they turn back while they still can.
what a scholar hears: the Qur'an's line on the timing of repentance, and the half-date hadith that makes the way out small and near.
recall: leaving others unable to match it
